# SQL Query: Budget by Department

Here are several SQL queries to retrieve budget information by department, ranging from simple to more advanced:

## Basic Query
```sql
SELECT 
    department_name,
    budget
FROM departments
ORDER BY budget DESC;
```

## Aggregated Budget (if budgets are stored per project/item)
```sql
SELECT 
    d.department_name,
    SUM(b.amount) AS total_budget
FROM departments d
JOIN budgets b ON d.department_id = b.department_id
GROUP BY d.department_name
ORDER BY total_budget DESC;
```

## Detailed Query with Multiple Metrics
```sql
SELECT 
    d.department_id,
    d.department_name,
    SUM(b.allocated_amount) AS total_allocated,
    SUM(b.spent_amount) AS total_spent,
    SUM(b.allocated_amount - b.spent_amount) AS remaining_budget,
    ROUND((SUM(b.spent_amount) / NULLIF(SUM(b.allocated_amount), 0)) * 100, 2) AS percent_used
FROM departments d
LEFT JOIN budgets b ON d.department_id = b.department_id
GROUP BY d.department_id, d.department_name
ORDER BY total_allocated DESC;
```

## Filtered by Fiscal Year
```sql
SELECT 
    d.department_name,
    b.fiscal_year,
    SUM(b.amount) AS annual_budget
FROM departments d
JOIN budgets b ON d.department_id = b.department_id
WHERE b.fiscal_year = 2024
GROUP BY d.department_name, b.fiscal_year
ORDER BY annual_budget DESC;
```

## With Percentage of Total Company Budget
```sql
SELECT 
    d.department_name,
    SUM(b.amount) AS dept_budget,
    ROUND(SUM(b.amount) * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(amount) FROM budgets), 2) AS pct_of_total
FROM departments d
JOIN budgets b ON d.department_id = b.department_id
GROUP BY d.department_name
ORDER BY dept_budget DESC;
```

**Note:** Adjust the table names (`departments`, `budgets`) and column names (`department_id`, `amount`, etc.) to match your actual database schema. If you share your table structure, I can tailor the query precisely.
